en: Having completed the repentance for all offenses committed by body, speech, and mind, I take refuge and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
With a sincere heart, I entreat the Buddhas of the ten directions who are currently attaining enlightenment: "I pray that you turn the Wheel of Dharma to bring peace and happiness to all beings."

I prostrate with my face cast down before all the Buddhas of the ten directions, entreating them that they would not relinquish their life-force but remain for a long time. Having made this entreaty, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem. With a sincere heart, I rejoice in all the merit of giving.
The upholding of precepts and the cultivation of meditative concentration and wisdom arise from body, speech, and mind.

May all those who have studied the Three Vehicles in the past, future, and present, as well as those who fully possess the One Vehicle, and the immeasurable multitudes of humans and devas with merit, all rejoice in this.
Having rejoiced, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem. With a sincere mind, I dedicate the merit of all my performed deeds toward the liberation of all sentient beings.
One should correctly dedicate [merit] toward the Buddha-way;
transgressions should be repented in this manner.
One should exhort [the Buddhas], rejoice [in merit], and dedicate the blessings toward Bodhi.
Having performed the dedication, I take refuge and pay homage to the Triple Gem. With a sincere mind, I make this vow: may all sentient beings alike resolve to attain bodhicitta.
May they fix their minds and constantly contemplate all Buddhas of the ten directions.
Furthermore, I vow that all sentient beings shall forever shatter all afflictions and clearly perceive the Buddha-nature, just like Mañjuśrī and others.
Having made this vow, they take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
I address all sentient beings: listen to this verse of purity for the early morning. Those who seek the bliss of nirvana should study the Dharma of the śramaṇa.
Food and clothing merely sustain the physical life.
Whether refined or coarse, may you all be equal.
This morning at dawn, having purified yourselves, each of you should maintain the six recollections:
mindfulness of the Buddha, mindfulness of the Dharma, mindfulness of the Sangha, mindfulness of the precepts, mindfulness of the devas, and mindfulness of generosity.
The invocation of the Buddha and the ritual for the Dharma shall follow the preceding text.
Furthermore, the verse for the evening twilight: The sun has already set in the western quarter, yet the afflictions of dust and toil have not yet been removed.
The time for old age, sickness, and death has arrived;
we shall not remain together for long.
Moment by moment, life is driven forward and its span shortened.
Like fish in scanty water,
I exhort all those who practice the Path to cultivate their training until reaching the state of Nirvana without remainder.
Verses on Impermanence at Midnight: Each person should individually contemplate the state of their own body:
The bones, flesh, sinews, and skin are a mixture of the light and the solid;
Earth, water, fire, and wind combine to form this provisional body.
The four great elements disperse, originally having no master;
a single casket of putrid flesh turns into a carbuncle.
Broken apart and rotting, it follows the dust and ashes.
The Verse on Impermanence from the Final Watch of the Night: Time flows like a thousand currents;
suddenly the first watch of the fifth watch arrives.
Impermanence reaches us moment by moment.
Constantly dwelling with the King of Death,
I exhort all those who practice the Path to cultivate their training until reaching the state of Nirvana without remainder.
Repentance of the Six Faculties: Since immeasurable kalpas past, we have constantly been deceived by the six thieves.
Dwelling within the state of non-duality, we have collectively given rise to discrimination.
The faculty of the eye has always craved forms.
The ears discriminate sounds;
the nose is deluded by and attached to other fragrances;
the tongue is constantly greedy for various flavors.
The body constantly delights in the sensation of touch,
and the mind universally grasps at objects;
thus, this inverted state of mind remains firm.
Sinking into the ocean of birth and death,
having already performed repentance, I take refuge and pay homage to the Three [Jewels]. May we, from this day forth until the realization of Bodhi,
have the six enemies constantly transformed into the six supernatural powers.
The three poisons are transformed into the three gates of liberation;
they are identical within the awakening to the equality of true suchness.
Without abandoning birth and death, one realizes nirvana.
Constantly rescuing sentient beings throughout the six realms of existence, may we together realize the unsurpassed path of the Tathāgata.
With a sincere heart, I make this vow: May my faculty of sight always behold the Buddha.
May my ears always hear the sound of the Dharma being preached;
may my nose never smell any other fragrance;
may my mouth constantly recite the *pāramitās*.
May my body remain unstained by all erroneous objects;
may my will not cling to conditioned phenomena with signs;
may my mind be able to eliminate the thieves of affliction.
May I always reach the city of Nirvana.
May I vow that all sentient beings attain Buddhahood.
May I vow to universally realize the causes of Nirvana.
Having made these vows, I take refuge and pay homage to the Triple Gem: Sentient beings are boundless; I vow to deliver them all.
Afflictions are boundless; I vow to sever them all.
Dharma gates are inexhaustible; I vow to study them all.
I vow to accomplish the unsurpassed path of the Buddha.
Listen to this verse on knowing the impermanence of time: If desire and form do not abide, the movement of grass stains all with dust.
Following conditions, it wanders through the six realms;
in a single kṣaṇa, it does not remain bound.
Know that the body is like a flash of lightning.
Realization is like drifting clouds;
having understood that the mind is fundamentally pure,
one turns one's vows toward entry into the gateway of truth.
